evidence.quote: Today, the FOMC decided to leave our policy interest rate unchanged and to continue to reduce our securities holdings.
So far this year, the data have not given us that greater confidence.
So the sense of that is that rate cuts that might take place in—might’ve taken place this year—take place next year, you know?
Inflation has eased substantially from a peak of 7 percent to 2.7 percent but is still too high.
As labor market tightness has eased and inflation has declined over the past year, the risks to achieving our employment and inflation goals have moved toward better balance.
So, overall, we’re looking at what is still a very strong labor market but not the superheated labor market of two years ago or even one year ago.

parsed.rationale: The Fed holds at a restrictive level, says the data have not yet given enough confidence to cut, and notes that cuts have shifted later, which leans modestly hawkish. That lean is offset by welcoming the soft CPI reading, describing risks as moving toward balance, and remaining open to cuts if the labor market weakens.
